selection_method: Purposive editorial sample of observable structures; not a performance-ranked or representative sample. Eight authors; English business/technology emphasis.
rights_note: Linked source posts remain with their respective rights holders. No source-post body, image, comment archive or third-party template collection is bundled.

examples.author: April Dunford
examples.label: AI and the positioning decision
examples.structure_note: Two decision questions separate customer value from a technology trend.
examples.adaptable_principle: Use explicit decision criteria before offering a recommendation.
examples.limitations: The author's claims and terminology are reference material, not the client's positioning.

examples.author: April Dunford
examples.label: Sell the capability available now
examples.structure_note: A positioning principle is developed through the difference between an investor's future interest and a buyer's present need.
examples.adaptable_principle: Connect an abstract principle to a buyer's actual decision.
examples.limitations: Do not repeat present-tense product or economic claims from an old post without checking.

examples.author: April Dunford
examples.label: Identify the customer's actual alternatives
examples.structure_note: A memorable problem definition leads to a distinction between current buyer alternatives and possible future competitors.
examples.adaptable_principle: Define the boundary of a comparison before recommending action.
examples.limitations: Use a fresh explanation; do not appropriate the author's distinctive label or claimed client observations.

examples.author: April Dunford
examples.label: Diagnose an apparent lack of differentiation
examples.structure_note: A reader question is divided into two possible diagnoses, followed by explanations of why a team might miss existing value.
examples.adaptable_principle: Answer directly, then branch according to evidence instead of giving one universal prescription.
examples.limitations: The diagnoses are the author's view; they are not evidence about the current client.

examples.author: April Dunford
examples.label: Separate strategy, vision and current positioning
examples.structure_note: A clear position is supported by two consequences and a distinction between present value and a future direction.
examples.adaptable_principle: Make reasoning inspectable by showing what a mistaken decision would change.
examples.limitations: Do not convert hypothetical future capabilities into shipped product claims.

examples.author: April Dunford
examples.label: A book announcement with a buyer problem
examples.structure_note: The announcement connects earlier work to a remaining buyer problem, then explains the purpose of the new book.
examples.adaptable_principle: Explain why an offer exists before asking for attention.
examples.limitations: Book dates, experience and customer claims belong to the source author; launch timing is historical.

examples.author: Amanda Natividad
examples.label: Audience research as the mechanism behind a case
examples.structure_note: A first-person work example moves from reported outcomes to audience research practices, then to a relevant workshop invitation.
examples.adaptable_principle: Show the mechanism between an activity and a proposed lesson; make an invitation follow useful content.
examples.limitations: Reported business results were not independently audited. Never transfer them to a client or claim causal proof.

examples.author: Amanda Natividad
examples.label: Career reintroduction through working beliefs
examples.structure_note: An audience milestone introduces a career path; selected experiences lead into working beliefs and a reader question.
examples.adaptable_principle: Use relevant biographical details to explain a point of view rather than listing credentials.
examples.limitations: The biography, milestone and role are historical source claims, not transferable facts.

examples.author: Jason Fried
examples.label: A product preview with unresolved work
examples.structure_note: The caption identifies a work-in-progress product, describes one view, acknowledges unknowns and invites questions.
examples.adaptable_principle: A real artifact can make progress concrete while preserving uncertainty.
examples.limitations: Only public caption/text was inspected; the video was not independently watched or product-tested.

examples.author: Jason Fried
examples.label: A demo experience becomes a product principle
examples.structure_note: A specific internal presentation leads to self-critique and an explanation of the author's product-development preference.
examples.adaptable_principle: Connect a real moment, a decision and a bounded personal principle.
examples.limitations: Do not copy the author's coined terminology, meeting scene or preference as the client's.

examples.author: Jason Fried
examples.label: Defend a product focus through analogy
examples.structure_note: A criticism of repeated product categories is acknowledged before craft analogies are used to explain the author's perspective.
examples.adaptable_principle: Treat an objection fairly and use an original analogy to clarify a deliberate choice.
examples.limitations: Quoted collaborators, distinctive analogies and personal motivation remain the source author's.

examples.author: Jason Fried
examples.label: Disagreement as part of making a product
examples.structure_note: A first-person comparison leads into a view about human disagreement and product work, supported by a named collaboration.
examples.adaptable_principle: A supported personal stance can end on a clear principle without an engagement question.
examples.limitations: This is a viewpoint, not a measured claim about AI or an experience the client can inherit.

examples.author: Molly Graham
examples.label: A management bottleneck reveals unclear criteria
examples.structure_note: A recognizable management problem introduces an attributed guest example and a lesson about making judgment explicit.
examples.adaptable_principle: Keep the speaker and experience owner clear when turning an interview into a lesson.
examples.limitations: The guest's experience is attributed; the client did not necessarily have this conversation.

examples.author: Molly Graham
examples.label: An operator community explained through real decisions
examples.structure_note: Concrete leadership questions make the need for a community specific before an application invitation.
examples.adaptable_principle: Describe the situations an offer helps with and connect the next step to those situations.
examples.limitations: The cohort deadline and offer availability are historical, not current recommendations.

examples.author: Molly Graham
examples.label: Where to invest management attention
examples.structure_note: A common management approach is challenged with the author's stated priority and reasoning about growth opportunities.
examples.adaptable_principle: Link an explicit working belief to a concrete allocation of attention.
examples.limitations: Career outcomes and retention implications are source assertions, not independently established causal findings.

examples.author: Molly Graham
examples.label: Separate a difficult decision from its handling
examples.structure_note: A difficult organizational decision is normalized, then contrasted with the care or carelessness of its execution.
examples.adaptable_principle: Make room for an unavoidable decision while specifying the responsibilities around it.
examples.limitations: No named employee situation was independently verified; do not invent an analogous client story.

examples.author: Katelyn Bourgoin
examples.label: A compact buyer-understanding argument
examples.structure_note: A short reader question is followed by a proposed relationship between recognition, trust and purchase.
examples.adaptable_principle: A narrow point can work as a compact post without a long list or story.
examples.limitations: The trust-to-sales link is an argument, not a measured conversion guarantee.

examples.author: Katelyn Bourgoin
examples.label: A future goal leads into learned priorities
examples.structure_note: A stated business goal and retrospective context introduce a numbered set of audience-building lessons.
examples.adaptable_principle: Keep future intention separate from reported history, then tie reflection to practical priorities.
examples.limitations: Revenue targets, audience counts and personal history are unverified source assertions; do not copy them.

examples.author: Katelyn Bourgoin
examples.label: A reader problem introduces relevant experts
examples.structure_note: A warning about buyer indifference leads to a curated set of people, with a reason to consider each.
examples.adaptable_principle: Make curation useful by giving selection criteria and reader-specific reasons.
examples.limitations: Source endorsements are not the client's endorsements; verify current resources before recommending.

examples.author: Rand Fishkin
examples.label: Clarify the implications of a marketing change
examples.structure_note: The caption lists possible overreactions to a change, rejects them and introduces adaptation as the topic.
examples.adaptable_principle: Separate a real change from conclusions that do not follow from it.
examples.limitations: Caption and public transcript text were inspected; the video was not watched and claims need fresh verification.

examples.author: Rand Fishkin
examples.label: Explain confusion about a research result
examples.structure_note: The caption addresses confusion about a published study; the available transcript explains measurements and points toward methodology.
examples.adaptable_principle: Treat a disputed number as a prompt to clarify units, scope and method.
examples.limitations: The study was not independently replicated; transcript wording can contain errors and figures are historical.

examples.author: Rand Fishkin
examples.label: Preview an educational resource by its questions
examples.structure_note: A resource announcement lists the questions the lesson covers and identifies its format.
examples.adaptable_principle: State the learning job of a resource so the reader can judge relevance.
examples.limitations: Do not adopt source claims about platform algorithms or link placement as current rules.

examples.author: Gergely Orosz
examples.label: Connect a technology claim to an organizational decision
examples.structure_note: A view about AI and engineering culture is connected to the role of management and a pointed organizational question.
examples.adaptable_principle: Make the practical tension explicit rather than ending with generic agreement bait.
examples.limitations: The organizational prediction is a viewpoint; no causal study or particular company diagnosis was verified.

examples.author: Lenny Rachitsky
examples.label: Introduce a guest's idea with clear attribution
examples.structure_note: A short caption attributes an idea to an interview guest; the public transcript expands the product-work context.
examples.adaptable_principle: A repurposed interview needs clear ownership of the idea even when the caption is short.
examples.limitations: Text/transcript only; speaker wording may be transcribed imperfectly. No Kleo authorship was established.
